title: Framework responds to complaints that BIOS update bricks Ryzen 7040 laptops
gist: A June 2026 BIOS update for Framework's Ryzen 7040 laptops is bricking a portion of units, a recurring defect pattern dating back to March 2025, prompting Framework to build a 'Crisis Recovery Mode' and selectively extend free out-of-warranty repairs.

insights.claim: A June 2026 BIOS 3.20 update for Framework Laptop 13 (Ryzen 7040 series) has been bricking a 'small percentage' of units, per Framework's own admission, with the company still investigating the root cause as of publication.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: A recurring firmware-reliability issue for a right-to-repair-focused hardware brand; customers should watch whether the stated fix and forthcoming recovery mode actually resolve the defect before further BIOS rollouts.
insights.quote: received reports of a small percentage of Framework Laptop 13 7040 Series BIOS updates resulting in non-bootable boards
insights.locator: In a company statement, Framework said

insights.claim: Reports of Ryzen 7040 Framework Laptop 13 BIOS-update failures date back to at least March 2025, indicating this is a recurring, unresolved defect pattern rather than an isolated incident tied to the June 2026 update.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Signals a longer-running quality-control issue that predates the current incident, relevant to assessing whether Framework's promised fixes will actually be durable.
insights.locator: There are reports of users having problems with BIOS upgrades

insights.claim: Framework is introducing a 'Crisis Recovery Mode' to make future failed BIOS updates directly recoverable, first shipping on the Framework Desktop with laptop 12/13/16 support to follow in upcoming release cycles, an admission that the current update mechanism lacks robust failure recovery.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: A structural fix that, if delivered, should reduce future bricking risk from firmware updates across Framework's laptop lineup.
insights.quote: Our latest Framework Desktop BIOS release includes this functionality, and we are actively bringing it to Framework Laptop 12, 13, and 16 in our upcoming BIOS release cycles for each

insights.claim: Framework is granting free out-of-warranty motherboard replacements only where it can confirm a stable-release BIOS update caused the board to become non-bootable, after some customers reported being denied free repairs and told to buy a new motherboard.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Selective, discretionary warranty remediation is a reputational risk for a company whose brand is built on repairability and customer trust.
insights.quote: in addition to replacing in-warranty Mainboards, we are making exceptions for out-of-warranty replacements where we can confirm a stable-release BIOS update caused the board to become non-bootable
